_comment: T1 (05_meeting01_t1_transformer.py), arm A (control), eegmmidb fold 0, config c2 = {"d_model": 79, "d_ff": 105, "n_heads": 1, "n_layers": 1}: the Transformer-AE winner of GridUnesp job 5317827 for seed 43. The pre-validation profile with the NSGA-II pinned to this genome (population 1, 0 generations, winner_seeds 1), one dataset, the direct code, the arm's switch.

experiment._repeats_comment: 2 seeds (42, 43): enough to see whether a family's result is one seed's luck, at a fraction of the grid's 5.

dataset._loso_max_train_windows_comment: 1000 since 2026-11-02 (was 200; author's decision): the format-5 design was diagnosed and validated at 1000 training windows per fold, and more windows improve every model (FSDD fold 0, C++, format 4: SNN-AE 0.880 -> 0.827, ann-ae 0.706 -> 0.662 from 200 to 1000) without closing the SNN-AE / ann-ae gap.
dataset._latex_data_dir_comment: Empty, as in meeting01-loso.json: the four family processes share a run tag, so their per-fold LaTeX exports had the same names and overwrote each other in the paper's data/ (found by the smoke test, 2026-11-02); nothing reads them.

sources.name: fsdd
sources._latent_dim_comment: 16 (16:1 vs the 256-sample window): short-speech/traditional AE and LSTM bottlenecks in the literature sit at 8-16 -- see .wiki/Experiments/Meeting01.md.

sources.name: audiomnist
sources._latent_dim_comment: 16 (16:1): same short-speech domain as fsdd; AudioMNIST encoders in the literature sit in the 16-64 range -- see .wiki/Experiments/Meeting01.md.

sources._comment: Source: PhysioNet EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, https://physionet.org/content/eegmmidb/1.0.0/ (109 subjects, 64 channels, EDF+, one subdirectory per subject: S001/S001R01.edf ...). Downloaded 2026-11-01 (1526 EDF, 3.4 GB). Signal 0 of each .edf is read; verified 2026-11-04 against the headers of all 1526 files to be the EEG channel 'Fc5.', not an annotation/status channel: 1490 files at 160 Hz, 36 at 128 Hz (subjects S088, S092, S100). sample_rate is the rate all windows are cut at: each file is filtered at its own rate and converted (Meeting01Eeg.hpp).
sources.name: eegmmidb
sources._latent_dim_comment: 64 (4:1): no eegmmidb-specific AE paper found; extrapolated from Khan et al. 2023's shallow-AE result on CHB-MIT (a related but different seizure-EEG dataset, not used in this study) -- see .wiki/Experiments/Meeting01.md.

sources._comment: Source: Siena Scalp EEG Database, https://physionet.org/content/siena-scalp-eeg/1.0.0/ (Detti 2020; 14 subjects, up to 35 channels, 512 Hz, EDF, one subdirectory per subject: PN00/PN00-1.edf ...). Signal 0 of each .edf verified 2026-09-23 against real downloaded headers to be an EEG channel ("EEG Fp1"), not a status/EKG channel. Replaces CHB-MIT (2026-09-23): CHB-MIT's 42.6GB total did not fit available disk; Siena is a complete dataset in the same task category (seizure scalp EEG) at 20.3GB.
sources.name: siena
sources._latent_dim_comment: 64 (4:1, same as eegmmidb -- window_size=256 is global, not per-sample-rate): no Siena-specific AE paper found; extrapolated from Khan et al. 2023's shallow-AE result on CHB-MIT (hidden_size=64; a separate {32,64,128} sweep on CHB-MIT also picked 64) -- same seizure-EEG task category as Siena, not a direct hit -- see .wiki/Experiments/Meeting01.md.

dataset._save_models_comment: false: the pre-validation reports costs and errors, it ships no model.

training._early_stop_min_skill_comment: Patience (early_stop_patience) only counts once the monitor loss is at most (1 - this) x the loss of the mean-target predictor; until then the run cannot stop early, and the best monitor epoch's network is kept (results_format 7). 0.10: the deepest plateau excursion in the pre-validation's 216 trainings was a skill of 0.066. Rationale: lib/include/Meeting01Stopping.hpp.

model._latent_dim_comment: Fallback only: every dataset in evaluation.datasets below overrides this via dataset.sources[].latent_dim (16 audio / 64 EEG), so this value is never actually read by the LOSO grid -- kept as a sane default for ad-hoc single-dataset runs of this profile with --dataset omitted-override.
model._time_steps_comment: Not set here since 2026-11-02: T is a gene of the SNN-AE search (evaluation.ga.snn.time_steps_min/max), so model.time_steps would be a value no SNN reads. History: 16 until 2026-11-01, then 4 from FSDD alone; on eegmmidb fold 0 T = 16 beat T = 4 by ~0.05 (validation 0.372 vs 0.425), on FSDD T made no difference, so the author made T a free gene chosen on validation per fold.
model._lstm_frame_size_comment: 8 = the binary's default, which the grid profile read before 2026-11-02 without declaring it. Declared here because the paper states the sequence the three families read: S = window_size * recurrent_time_steps / lstm_frame_size = 256 * 1 / 8 = 32 frames of 8 samples (00_meeting01_prevalidation_report.py refuses a profile without it).
model._snn_time_pool_comment: latent (2026-11-01): the SNN-AE averages its latent over the T steps and runs its decoder once. Gap diagnosis (.wiki/Experiments/Meeting01.md, 'Where the gap comes from'): scoring every step's output costs ~0.05 test MSE; averaging at the latent or at the output measured the same (0.724 vs 0.724 at T = 4), and the latent is T x cheaper in the decoder.
model._snn_decoder_neuron_comment: analog (2026-11-01): leaky ReLU in the decoder, the neuron ann-ae's decoder has, so the SNN-AE and the ann-ae control differ in the encoder's hidden neuron alone (LIF over T steps vs leaky ReLU once). Required by snn_time_pool = latent.
model._initializer_comment: xavier (2026-11-01) for the SNN-AE and, when it runs, its matched control ann-ae (validate() requires the field once ann-ae is a baseline). Left empty each builder kept its own -- kaiming SNN, xavier ANN -- so the control differed in its starting weights too. PyTorch twin, 3 seeds, test MSE kaiming -> xavier: eegmmidb fold 0 ANN 0.489 -> 0.293, SNN-AE (this design) 0.484 -> 0.449; FSDD fold 0 ANN 0.667 -> 0.654, SNN-AE 0.724 -> 0.729. Xavier is better or equal for both arms on both datasets; the ANN's kaiming deficit on EEG persists to convergence (200-epoch cap: 0.479 vs 0.291).

evaluation._baselines_comment: All four; 00_meeting01_prevalidate_baselines.sh narrows each process to one family (ann-ae always with the SNN arm, whose winner it copies).

snn._time_steps_comment: T, an integer drawn uniformly in [2, 32] (author's decision 2026-11-02: a free range, not preset values). 2 is the least validate() accepts (one step leaves alpha and the poisson/latency codes without a time axis); 32 is twice the largest T measured on EEG (16, the best there). The GA's cost objective (estimate_snn_macs) grows with T: every layer runs at every step, except that a direct-coded input through dense/conv1d has its first layer counted once (results_format 9, the energy_nj rule); it keeps cheaper genomes on the Pareto front, but the winner is the front's lowest re-scored validation MSE (cost only breaks ties), so a longer T is selected only when it validates better.

ga._budget_comment: Reduced and identical for all five families (4 x (1 + 2) = 12 search evaluations, the front re-scored with 2 seeds), against the grid's 8 x (1 + 5) = 48 with 3: a pre-validation, not a search of record. Bounds are the grid's.
